video_title: Castle CALLS OUT Refs - Did They Cost Spurs The Game?!?

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: OKC's deep bench and role players like Jared McCain and Alex Caruso
quotes.excerpt: This team can go to guy after guy after guy and get something out of them and to be able to write the ship
quotes.quote: I don't think Jared McCain has found a shot that he doesn't like yet. When you talk about a guy that's just ultra-aggressive, has the ultimate green light on a team that he's coming too late that he wasn't a part of this initial group, but him come in and fit in this way and be a scoring punch that they needed and to be inserted into the starting lineup his first playoff game to be able to start and him to have the game that he had was amazing. Alex Caruso, what his impact has been on both ends of the floor has been consistent throughout the playoffs and especially in this series. This team can go to guy after guy after guy and get something out of them and to be able to write the ship even when you feel like it's not going to be right with guys in and out of the lineup and that's is one of their best strengths this year. No team has been able to use that against them. Two games ago I've said it, they played 11 guys in the first quarter. That should tell you everything about the makeup of this group. But they go so deep in their bench, they just continue to plug and play guys. I think they got a piece of that from the team that they're playing against kind of using that strategy against them to be able to plug and play guys and having a strong system and a background that they can fall to and that's how they've been able to play throughout the course of this run against San Antonio.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Jared McCain's confidence and OKC's plug-and-play bench depth
quotes.excerpt: It's just crazy how good and how much bench depth that this team has and it really is the definition of a plug and play.
quotes.quote: When talking about Jared McCain, do you know how comfortable and confident you have to be to get traded mid-season to any team and go and play with the kind of confidence and rhythm that he's playing with? Let alone the Oklahoma City Thunder who are the best team in the NBA and he just gets traded in and just fits in right away and becomes an immediate huge part of their offense. They're such a great system where it doesn't matter if he's starting, if he got a DMP the night before, if he played 15 minutes or 30 minutes, the guy is the same consistent player. Lou mentioned Alex Caruso has been phenomenal. Cason Wallace we haven't even talked about very much. He's a starting shooting guard on pretty much every other team in the NBA. AJ Mitchell was the second leading scorer on this team in the playoffs and he's been a non-factor in the conference finals. It's just crazy how good and how much bench depth that this team has and it really is the definition of a plug and play.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Sixers' regret over trading Jared McCain and Daryl Morey's "selling high" claim
quotes.excerpt: I don't think that's accurate, you guys. I don't think that that's true and I think they're going to regret this for quite some time.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: Daryl Morey claiming that when he pulled this trade off that he was selling high. I don't think that's accurate, you guys. Chandler, I don't think that that's true and I think they're going to regret this for quite some time.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: Well, Daryl Morey got fired. This Jared McCain trade really never made sense from it. This is a guy that was runaway Rookie of the Year, I always talk about this, and then he got hurt. But he dominated 75% of this season scoring, doing exactly what he did now on a worse team with more opportunity.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: I don't know what Daryl Morey was thinking when he made this trade. Now you look at a Philadelphia team that needed another small guard, that needed somebody to be aggressive on the offensive end and to play with energy in a playoff series where you ran out of gas. This stuff starts to become a blinking light where you're like, wait a minute, so why did we trade him again? Why did we get rid of this guy again? And now he's showing you what his worth is on the biggest stage in the world. He's one game away from getting to a championship game and he's been a big focal point of them having success in this playoff. So will this be something that haunts Philly for years to come?

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: OKC's allowed physicality and the "art form" of drawing fouls
quotes.excerpt: I always think the more physical team gets away with more contact and more physicality.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: Is there just to the naked eye watching these games, does it feel to you like OKC is just allowed a little more physicality than perhaps San Antonio has been?

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: Maybe sometimes, but I always think the more physical team gets away with more contact and more physicality. That's just how you're coached. If you're going to dog someone 94 feet, a lot of times you get the benefit of the doubt of the whistle. That's what coaches always emphasize saying, hey, you be physical, you bring the fight to them, you throw the first punch because you they never catch the first guy, right? And so I think they do get away with some stuff just because of the physicality they play with.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: I think both teams are playing physical. I think both teams are doing a great job of getting to the free-throw line. And I've always said it, that is an art form. Only a certain type of player can be afforded to get to the free-throw line at the clip that an SGA does. Wemby is another one of those guys that can get to the free-throw line and understands we're playing a game inside of a game.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Referee inconsistency and missed calls impacting the series
quotes.excerpt: I just think the inconsistency is frustrating as a player. Some of the tick-tack calls were pretty bad.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: I was going to say. And they weren't fouls they missed.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: I watched the goaltend. I was like, that is a clear goaltend. How was that not called? Mitch Johnson asking for a challenge in front of the referee's face. That was clear. Some of these things were clear.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: That's crazy. That's nuts. In a stage of this and the magnitude of this game, it's tough to think you can miss a call like that. But again, that's just a blown call. That happens both ways, it happens all the time. I just think the inconsistency is frustrating as a player. Some of the tick-tack calls were pretty bad and it's just a tough watch honestly as an NBA fan. You don't want to see 70 free throws taken, the whistle just constantly blowing. You always hear the term playoff basketball, how it's more physical and then the refs sometimes call a tick-tack foul and then sometimes they don't. So I see both sides, I see the frustration.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: OKC's foul-drawing strategy making them unlikable to other fans
quotes.excerpt: Do you know how unlikable you have to be to the rest of the country when they're going to root for the Knicks because they cannot root for the Thunder in good conscience?

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: Do you know how unlikable you have to be to the rest of the country when they're going to root for the Knicks because they cannot root for the Thunder in good conscience? Like that is a crazy twist for you.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: If they worried about flopping, this is going to be a flop-a-thon if it's with the Knicks if this goes through. I don't qualify it as flopping. I think it's foul drawing. You're drawing fouls. I don't have a reputation as a flopper. I have a reputation as somebody that draws fouls. Big difference. I showed him a couple little things, I'm sure that he visually he picked up on some things and he flipped it to his liking, but again, if I know I'm in the bonus at seven and a half minutes in a game, the defender should know that as well. Back up a little bit. You should know that as well.
